resale_co.name: Code Compliance Inspection Certificate (CCIC) for sales
resale_co.issued_by: Township of Ocean Division of Housing, Code Enforcement and Clean Communities (Housing Inspector / Code Enforcement Official)
resale_co.lead_time: The Township must inspect and issue the CCIC or a notice of violation within 10 business days of the application.
resale_co.valid_for: If a Certificate of Transfer of Title is used first, a CCIC inspection within 90 days of the original inspection is billed as a reinspection; after 90 days a new application is needed.
requirements: Exterior and interior inspection under the International Property Maintenance Code (paint and siding, gutters, house number at least 4 inches, Township garbage and recycling containers, handrails, pool barriers, GFCI outlets, egress locks, bedroom doors)
All building permits must be closed before calling for the CCIC inspection
Smoke certification from your fire district must be submitted to the housing office before the certificate is issued
Septic or well report from the Monmouth County Health Department where the home is on a septic system or well; certified lab water test for wells
Level 1 fireplace or chimney inspection by a licensed chimney sweep
All utilities on at the time of inspection
Cracked sidewalks along the street must be repaired to the Municipal Engineer's requirements
Garage apartments or 2-family use need paperwork showing they are legal; finished third floors or attics will not pass without it

fees.label: CCIC for resale of a detached dwelling, applied and paid online
fees.quote: A nonrefundable fee of $150 shall be charged to cover the cost of application which is filled out and paid for online, which includes an inspection in connection with a resale of a detached dwelling unit.

fees.label: CCIC for resale of an attached single-family dwelling, applied and paid online
fees.quote: A nonrefundable fee of $125 shall be charged to cover the cost of application which is filled out and paid for online, which includes an inspection, in connection with a resale of an attached single-family dwelling unit.

fees.label: CCIC for resale of a detached dwelling, paper application
fees.quote: A nonrefundable fee of $175 shall be charged to cover the cost of inspection in connection with a resale of a detached dwelling unit.

fees.label: CCIC for resale of an attached single-family dwelling, paper application
fees.quote: A nonrefundable fee of $150 shall be charged to cover the cost of inspection in connection with a resale of an attached single-family dwelling unit.

fees.label: Reinspection when utilities are off, and second or later reinspections (first reinspection is free if utilities are on)
fees.quote: A reinspection fee of $75 shall be required for all reinspections where the utilities are not operational and for all second and subsequent reinspections for sales, rentals, and reoccupancy of single-family dwellings and/or title only transfers.

fees.label: Extra charge if utilities are not on at the inspection (Township checklist)

resale_co.how_to_apply: Apply online (cheaper) or on paper through the Township's Community Portal link on the Housing Forms page, then schedule with the Housing Division (732-531-5000 ext. 3392, oceancode@oceantwp.org). Close all building permits first. Before the certificate is issued, submit the smoke/CO certificate from your fire district, any septic/well report, and the Level 1 chimney inspection report. Post-dated checks are not accepted. Office: 399 Monmouth Road, Oakhurst, Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
resale_co.contact_title: Code Enforcement Administrator (ext. 3378); Toni Severini, Administrative Secretary (ext. 3392)

evidence.quote: The Housing Division is responsible for conducting Code Compliance Inspection Certificate inspections on all new sales of homes, condos and townhouses and any rentals that change occupancy.
No one is allowed to occupy or move in without a Code Compliance Inspection Certificate being issued.
All permits (SALES) must be closed prior to calling for a Code Compliance Inspection Certificate inspection.
We cannot accept post-dated checks...they will be returned to you.
A new Code Compliance Inspection Certificate is required for every change in ownership or change in occupancy for every dwelling, apartment and/or there alike.
An inspection pursuant to this section shall be made and either a Code Compliance Inspection Certificate or a notice of violation shall be issued within 10 business days from the date of application.
Should the inspection be completed subsequent to the 90 days, a new application will be required to be completed for a Code Compliance Inspection Certificate.
Smoke certification (performed by your fire district)
Office: 732-531-5000 Ext 3392 - oceancode@oceantwp.org
Unless paperwork can be provided, garage apartments or 2-family houses are illegal, and finished
Code Enforcement Administrator

resale_co.notes: Township Code Section 7-3.3 (amended by Ord. No. 2465, June 6, 2024) requires a new Code Compliance Inspection Certificate for every change in ownership. Fees under Section 7-3.9 are lower when you apply and pay online ($150 detached, $125 attached) than on paper ($175 / $150). The code has no separate fee line for a 2-family resale, and the Township checklist says 2-family houses are illegal unless paperwork shows otherwise, so ask the Housing Division how a legal 2-family is billed. A Certificate of Transfer of Title (Section 7-3.12) lets a property transfer without occupancy. Staff names, titles and extensions are from the Housing personnel page; the Division page lists Toni Severini's extension 3392 with a typo in the area code (731). Ken Pieslak's email appears as Kpieslak@oceantwp.org. Landlord registration and the lead-safe program apply to rentals only.

requirements: Smoke alarms no older than 10 years; battery units must be 10-year sealed; UL listed

By construction year (Fire District #1 handout): before 1978 battery alarms on each level; 1978-1983 hardwired on each level; 1984-1990 interconnected hardwired with battery backup on each level; 1991 on interconnected hardwired with battery backup on each level and in all bedrooms
Smoke alarms within 10 feet of bedroom doors, near stairs; in 2-family homes in common hallways and at each stair landing
Carbon monoxide alarms on each sleeping level near bedroom doors in homes with fuel-burning devices or an attached garage
Central station alarm systems must be audible and testable and cannot replace required alarms
Secondary power source label ("CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER") within 18 inches of the main panel and meter for homes with generators, solar or batteries
Fire extinguisher no longer required in Ocean Township (Fire District #1 handout, 9-2025); the Township Code fee section still names it

fire_cert.notes: Ocean Township has two fire districts, each its own LEA (registry code D for Ocean Township (1) and (2)). Township Code Section 6-5.6 sets the smoke/CO certificate fees at $35 / $70 / $125 plus a $20 reinspection, lower than the state schedule; ecode360 shows the chapter amended as recently as Ord. No. 2529 (12-11-2025). Fire District #1's 9-2025 requirements handout (a scanned PDF, so its quotes cannot be machine-checked) names Craig Flannigan as Fire Marshal at 72 Larkin Place, office 732-222-2624, and says the fire extinguisher is no longer required in Ocean Township, consistent with P.L.2025, c.19; the Township Code fee section title still names the extinguisher. The state directory shows the District #2 entry (Tom Haege) on both Ocean Township pages, which looks like a directory quirk. The registry also lists an 'Ocean Township' with code S, which is Ocean Township in Ocean County, not this town.

other_items.label: Open building permits
other_items.detail: All permits must be closed before calling for the CCIC inspection; the Township reviews for open permits before issuing the certificate.

other_items.label: Septic and well
other_items.detail: Homes on septic or well need a Monmouth County Health Department report; well water must be tested by a certified lab and meet NJDEP standards.

other_items.label: Chimney inspection
other_items.detail: A Level 1 fireplace/chimney inspection report from a licensed chimney sweep must be submitted before the CCIC is issued.

other_items.label: Sidewalks
other_items.detail: Cracked sidewalks and public access along the street are the owner's responsibility and must be repaired to the Municipal Engineer's requirements (CCIC checklist item).

other_items.label: Certificate of Transfer of Title
other_items.detail: A transfer-of-title certificate allows the sale without occupancy; a CCIC is still needed before anyone moves in.

open_questions: What fee applies to the resale of a legal 2-family home (Section 7-3.9 lists only detached and attached single-family resales)?
